424	                 + (if $decision == "ask" or $decision == "deny" then {hook: "implement-gate", action: $decision, gate_mode: $gmode} else {} end) + $replay' \
425	                >> "$RUN_DIR/audit.jsonl" 2>/dev/null || true
426	        }
427	        case "$active_skill" in
428	            implement|/implement|bug|/bug|run|/run|simstim|/simstim)
429	                # Tighten-only (n17/n18): a model-authored implementation claim never
430	                # allows by itself — log it, then fall through to the heuristic check below
431	                log_model_signal heuristic
432	                ;;
433	            *)
434	                # Non-implementation skill: asks whatever the sanction (decided below, where deny can still apply)
435	                claim_ask=1
436	                ;;
437	        esac
438	    else
439	        # active_skill field absent despite the claims modifier — fall back to heuristic
440	        # Log the downgrade
441	        log_ts=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ 2>/dev/null) || log_ts="unknown"
442	        jq -nc \
443	            --arg ts "$log_ts" \
444	            --arg from "authoritative" \
445	            --arg to "heuristic" \
446	            --arg reason "active_skill field absent in hook input" \
447	            --argjson replay "$_ig_replay_json" \
448	            '{timestamp: $ts, event: "compliance.mode.fallback", from_mode: $from, to_mode: $to, reason: $reason} + $replay' \
449	            >> "$RUN_DIR/audit.jsonl" 2>/dev/null || true
450	    fi
451	    # Fall through to heuristic check below
452	fi
453	
454	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
455	# Heuristic mode: Is an /implement or /bug skill currently active?
456	# Check .run/sprint-plan-state.json, .run/simstim-state.json, .run/state.json
457	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
458	# True when the ISO-8601 timestamp $1 parses and is within 24 h (86400 s) of now, either side; empty or unparsable is stale
459	# (sprint-250 audit LOW-004: tighten-only; LOW-006: a future-dated stamp is not fresh forever)
460	_ig_fresh() {
461	    [[ -n "$1" ]] || return 1
462	    local now last_epoch
463	    now=$(date +%s 2>/dev/null) || return 1
464	    if type _date_to_epoch &>/dev/null; then
465	        last_epoch=$(_date_to_epoch "$1" 2>/dev/null) || last_epoch=""
466	    else
467	        last_epoch=$(date -d "$1" +%s 2>/dev/null || date -jf '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ' "$1" +%s 2>/dev/null) || last_epoch=""
468	    fi
469	    [[ "$last_epoch" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$now" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || return 1
470	    (( last_epoch > 0 && now - last_epoch <= 86400 && last_epoch - now <= 86400 ))
471	}
472	
473	# True when the ISO-8601 timestamp $2 parses, is at most $1 seconds old and at most 300 s ahead (clock skew);
474	# jq's fromdateiso8601 keeps it portable (no GNU date -d). Fractional seconds are dropped first
475	_ig_within() {
476	    [[ -n "$2" && "$1" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || return 1
477	    jq -en --arg t "$2" --argjson w "$1" \
478	        '($t | sub("\\.[0-9]+Z$"; "Z") | try fromdateiso8601 catch null) as $e | $e != null and (now - $e) <= $w and ($e - now) <= 300' \
479	        >/dev/null 2>&1
480	}
481	
482	# derived_at, when a cache carries one, must be within run_mode.stale_hours (cycle-129 D-4.1)
483	_ig_derived_ok() {
484	    local da
485	    da=$(jq -r '.derived_at // empty | strings' "$1" 2>/dev/null) || da=""
486	    [[ -z "$da" ]] && return 0
487	    _ig_within $(( gate_stale_hours * 3600 )) "$da"
488	}
489	
490	check_implementation_active() {
491	    # Check sprint-plan state
492	    if [[ -f "$RUN_DIR/sprint-plan-state.json" ]]; then
493	        local state plan_id last_activity
494	        state=$(jq -r '.state // empty' "$RUN_DIR/sprint-plan-state.json" 2>/dev/null) || return 1
495	        plan_id=$(jq -r '.plan_id // empty' "$RUN_DIR/sprint-plan-state.json" 2>/dev/null) || true
496	
497	        # Integrity: must have plan_id
498	        if [[ -z "$plan_id" ]]; then
499	            return 1
500	        fi
501	
502	        # Integrity: check staleness (within 24 h either side, via _ig_fresh); an absent or unparsable
503	        # last_activity is stale too (sprint-250 audit LOW-006: the check was skipped, so RUNNING + plan_id allowed)
504	        last_activity=$(jq -r '.timestamps.last_activity // empty' "$RUN_DIR/sprint-plan-state.json" 2>/dev/null) || last_activity=""
505	        if ! _ig_fresh "$last_activity"; then
506	            return 1  # Stale, future-dated or unstamped state
507	        fi
508	
509	        # A derived cache older than run_mode.stale_hours is not a run position (cycle-129 D-4.1)
510	        if ! _ig_derived_ok "$RUN_DIR/sprint-plan-state.json"; then
511	            return 1
512	        fi
513	
514	        if [[ "$state" == "RUNNING" ]]; then
515	            return 0
516	        fi
517	    fi
518	
519	    # Check simstim state; its writers (simstim-state.sh, simstim-orchestrator.sh) stamp .timestamps.last_activity,
520	    # and a stale or unstamped file falls through (LOW-004)
521	    if [[ -f "$RUN_DIR/simstim-state.json" ]]; then
522	        local phase simstim_activity
523	        phase=$(jq -r '.phase // empty' "$RUN_DIR/simstim-state.json" 2>/dev/null) || return 1
524	        simstim_activity=$(jq -r '.timestamps.last_activity // empty | strings' "$RUN_DIR/simstim-state.json" 2>/dev/null) || simstim_activity=""
525	        if [[ "$phase" == "implementation" ]] && _ig_fresh "$simstim_activity"; then
526	            return 0
527	        fi
528	    fi
529	
530	    # Check run state; run-mode stamps .timestamps.last_activity (state-schemas.md), .updated_at is the fallback
531	    # run-preflight.sh reads too; a stale or unstamped file falls through (LOW-004)
532	    if [[ -f "$RUN_DIR/state.json" ]]; then
533	        local run_state run_activity
534	        run_state=$(jq -r '.state // empty' "$RUN_DIR/state.json" 2>/dev/null) || return 1
535	        run_activity=$(jq -r '.timestamps.last_activity // .updated_at // empty | strings' "$RUN_DIR/state.json" 2>/dev/null) || run_activity=""
536	        if [[ "$run_state" == "RUNNING" ]] && _ig_fresh "$run_activity" && _ig_derived_ok "$RUN_DIR/state.json"; then
537	            return 0
538	        fi
539	    fi
540	
541	    return 1
542	}
543	
544	# The implementing skills' marker (run-checkpoint.sh mark): 0 fresh and well-formed, 1 absent, 2 stale or malformed
545	check_implement_marker() {
546	    local f="$RUN_DIR/implement-active.json" started
547	    [[ -f "$f" ]] || return 1
548	    jq -e '(.skill == "implement" or .skill == "bug") and (.sprint | type == "string" and test("^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,64}$"))' "$f" >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 2
549	    started=$(jq -r '.started_at // empty | strings' "$f" 2>/dev/null) || started=""
550	    _ig_within 7200 "$started" || return 2
551	    return 0
552	}
553	
554	# The derived run position for deny: known only when .run/sprint-plan-state.json parses and carries a derived_at
555	# within run_mode.stale_hours; sets position_state (display copy) or position_why
556	position_state=""
557	position_why=""
558	read_position() {
559	    local f="$RUN_DIR/sprint-plan-state.json" da st
560	    if [[ ! -f "$f" ]]; then position_why="cache missing"; return 1; fi
561	    if ! jq -e 'type == "object"' "$f" >/dev/null 2>&1; then position_why="cache unparseable"; return 1; fi
562	    da=$(jq -r '.derived_at // empty | strings' "$f" 2>/dev/null) || da=""
563	    if [[ -z "$da" ]]; then position_why="cache not derived"; return 1; fi
564	    if ! _ig_within $(( gate_stale_hours * 3600 )) "$da"; then position_why="cache older than run_mode.stale_hours"; return 1; fi
565	    st=$(jq -r '.state // .status // empty | strings' "$f" 2>/dev/null) || st=""
566	    position_state=$(strip_controls "${st:-unknown}")
567	    [[ -n "$position_state" ]] || position_state="unknown"
568	    return 0
569	}
570	
571	emit_deny() {
572	    jq -nc --arg r "$1" '{hookSpecificOutput:{hookEventName:"PreToolUse",permissionDecision:"deny",permissionDecisionReason:$r}}'
573	}
574	deny_reason() {
575	    printf 'App Zone write with no active implementation run (derived position: %s); run /implement or /bug, or set implement_gate.mode: ask' "$position_state"
576	}
577	
578	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
579	# Sanction: a fresh RUNNING cache, a fresh implementing-skill marker, or the
580	# operator's override, in that order — one row for the path that sanctioned
581	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
582	sanction=""
583	if check_implementation_active; then
584	    sanction="sanctioned_run"
585	else
586	    check_implement_marker
587	    marker_rc=$?
588	    if (( marker_rc == 0 )); then
589	        sanction="sanctioned_marker"
590	    elif [[ "${LOA_IMPLEMENT_GATE_OVERRIDE:-}" == "1" ]]; then
591	        sanction="override"
592	    fi
593	    (( marker_rc == 2 )) && log_gate_row note stale_marker
594	fi
595	
596	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
597	# A non-implementation claim asks whatever the sanction; under deny with a
598	# known position and no sanction it is denied (tighten-only: never looser)
599	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
600	if (( claim_ask )); then
601	    if [[ "$gate_mode" == "deny" && -z "$sanction" ]] && read_position; then
602	        echo "[AUTHORITATIVE] App Zone write to '$safe_file_path' denied during /$safe_skill (not an implementation skill; derived position: $position_state)." >&2
603	        log_model_signal deny
604	        emit_deny "$(deny_reason)"
605	        exit 0
606	    fi
607	    echo "[AUTHORITATIVE] App Zone write to '$safe_file_path' detected during /$safe_skill (not an implementation skill)." >&2
608	    log_model_signal ask
609	    emit_ask "[AUTHORITATIVE] App Zone write outside implementation skill. Verify this is intentional."
610	    exit 0
611	fi
612	
613	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
614	# Decision
615	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
616	if [[ -n "$sanction" ]]; then
617	    # Implementation is active (or the operator overrode) — allow the write, one row
618	    log_gate_row allow "$sanction"
619	    exit 0
620	fi
621	
622	case "$gate_mode" in
623	    telemetry)
624	        # Log and allow, silently
625	        log_gate_row telemetry outside_run
626	        exit 0
627	        ;;
628	    deny)
629	        if read_position; then
630	            echo "[GATE] App Zone write to '$safe_file_path' denied: no active implementation run (derived position: $position_state)." >&2
631	            log_gate_row deny deny
632	            emit_deny "$(deny_reason)"
633	            exit 0
634	        fi
635	        # Unknown position: ask, never allow
636	        echo "[GATE] App Zone write to '$safe_file_path' outside an active run; run position unknown ($position_why), asking instead of denying." >&2
637	        log_gate_row ask unknown_position
638	        emit_ask "[ADVISORY] App Zone write outside active implementation; run position unknown ($position_why). Verify this is intentional."
639	        exit 0
640	        ;;
641	    *)
642	        # No active implementation detected — ADVISORY ask (unchanged), now counted
643	        echo "[ADVISORY] App Zone write to '$safe_file_path' detected outside active /implement or /bug." >&2
644	        echo "No RUNNING state found in .run/ state files. This may bypass review gates." >&2
645	        log_gate_row ask ask
646	        echo '{"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"PreToolUse","permissionDecision":"ask","permissionDecisionReason":"[ADVISORY] App Zone write outside active implementation. Verify this is intentional."}}'
647	        exit 0
648	        ;;
649	esac

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# =============================================================================
3	# tools/check-knob-readers.sh — no direct read of a profile key outside
4	# profile-lib.sh (cycle-129 SDD D-9.1, sprint-256 Task 2.7).
5	#
6	# Every key under any profile in .claude/data/profiles.yaml must be read
7	# through `loa_knob` (.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh), never by a reader's
8	# own `yq '.<key> // <default>'`: a direct read skips the profile, and yq's
9	# `//` reads an explicit `false` as absent. The check flags a line that names a
10	# profile key in yq-path form (a leading dot: `.guardrails.input.enabled`)
11	# under .claude/ (scripts, hooks, skills, data) and tools/, except
12	# profile-lib.sh itself. Prose that names a key without the dot
13	# (`guardrails.input.enabled: false`) is not a read and is not flagged.
14	#
15	# Misses: a key assembled at runtime (".guardrails.input.${x}.enabled") and a
16	# reader in a language that indexes the config as nested keys.
17	#
18	# Usage: tools/check-knob-readers.sh [--root DIR]
19	# Exit:  0 clean · 1 direct read found (each printed as path:line) · 2 usage
20	# =============================================================================
21	set -euo pipefail
22	export LC_ALL=C
23	
24	ROOT="."
25	while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
26	  case "$1" in
27	    --root) [[ $# -ge 2 ]] || { echo "check-knob-readers.sh: --root needs a directory" >&2; exit 2; }; ROOT="$2"; shift 2 ;;
28	    -h|--help) sed -n '/^# Usage:/,/^# Exit:/p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; exit 0 ;;
29	    *) echo "check-knob-readers.sh: unknown arg $1" >&2; exit 2 ;;
30	  esac
31	done
32	PROFILES="$ROOT/.claude/data/profiles.yaml"
33	[[ -f "$PROFILES" ]] || { echo "check-knob-readers.sh: $PROFILES not found" >&2; exit 2; }
34	command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "check-knob-readers.sh: yq v4 required" >&2; exit 2; }
35	
36	keys=$(yq -r '.profiles[] | keys | .[]' "$PROFILES" | sort -u)
37	[[ -n "$keys" ]] || { echo "check-knob-readers.sh: no profile keys in $PROFILES" >&2; exit 2; }
38	# Alternation of the dot-escaped keys; each must be preceded by a dot that is
39	# not itself part of an identifier (start of line, quote, space, paren, ...).
40	alt=$(printf '%s\n' "$keys" | sed 's/\./\\./g' | paste -sd'|' -)
41	pattern="(^|[^A-Za-z0-9_])\\.(${alt})([^A-Za-z0-9_]|$)"
42	
43	hits=$(cd "$ROOT" && grep -rnE "$pattern" .claude tools 2>/dev/null \
44	  | grep -v -E '^(\./)?\.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib\.sh:' \
45	  | grep -v -E '^(\./)?tools/check-knob-readers\.sh:' || true)
46	if [[ -n "$hits" ]]; then
47	  echo "check-knob-readers.sh: direct read(s) of a profile key; use loa_knob from .claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh:" >&2
48	  printf '%s\n' "$hits" | cut -c1-240 >&2
49	  exit 1
50	fi
51	echo "check-knob-readers.sh: no direct profile-key reads ($(printf '%s\n' "$keys" | wc -l | tr -d ' ') keys checked)"

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# =============================================================================
3	# tools/check-prompt-budget.sh — byte budgets for the always-loaded prompt surface
4	#
5	# cycle-124 FR-8 (AC-8.1). The prompt surface Claude loads on every turn or on
6	# every skill invocation has hard byte budgets; this is the CI gate behind them.
7	#
8	#   .claude/skills/*/SKILL.md      ≤ 16,384 B  each — charged with every
9	#                                  resources/*.md the skill reads UNCONDITIONALLY
10	#   .claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md      ≤ 9,445 B (cycle-129 D-3.3: min(previous cap, measured 9,189 B + 256 B); the cap never rises)
11	#   .claude/protocols/*.md (total) ≤ 160,000 B fail; > 114,688 B warns (reference/ is not counted)
12	#
13	# Resource charging rule (the byte budget cannot be met by moving text into a
14	# file the skill still always loads): a resources/<name>.md is charged when a
15	# SKILL.md line names it AND reads as an unguarded read imperative —
16	#   imperative: (?i)\b(read|load|source|include)\b          e.g. "Read `resources/X.md`"
17	#   guard:      (?i)\b(if|when|only|optional|as needed|on demand|unless|may|see)\b
18	# A line with a guard word ("See resources/X.md §Security", "read X.md if …") is
19	# a pointer, not a load, and is not charged. Pinned by tests/unit/prompt-budget.bats.
20	#
21	# Every other SKILL.md figure the sprint report needs from the "mechanical pass"
22	# (history tokens per file) rides along in --json as `history_tokens` —
23	# informational; enforcement of that rule is tests/unit/no-history-in-rule-text.bats.
24	#
25	# Usage:
26	#   tools/check-prompt-budget.sh              # human table, exit 1 on any breach
27	#   tools/check-prompt-budget.sh --json       # machine-readable report
28	#   tools/check-prompt-budget.sh --root DIR   # check a fixture tree (tests / CI sentinels)
29	#   tools/check-prompt-budget.sh --quiet      # exit code only
30	#
31	# Exit codes: 0 within budget · 1 breach · 2 usage / missing root
32	# =============================================================================
33	set -euo pipefail
34	export LC_ALL=C
35	
36	ROOT="."
37	JSON=0
38	QUIET=0
39	while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
40	  case "$1" in
41	    --root) [[ $# -ge 2 ]] || { echo "check-prompt-budget.sh: --root needs a directory" >&2; exit 2; }; ROOT="$2"; shift 2 ;;
42	    --json) JSON=1; shift ;;
43	    --quiet|-q) QUIET=1; shift ;;
44	    --help|-h) sed -n '/^# Usage:/,/^# Exit codes/p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; exit 0 ;;
45	    *) echo "check-prompt-budget.sh: unknown arg $1" >&2; exit 2 ;;

55	GUARD = re.compile(r"\b(if|when|only|optional|as needed|on demand|unless|may|see)\b", re.I)

content.content:
**The contract (D-2.3).** When `rejected_summary` is non-empty the feedback file MUST contain a
`## Rejected dissent payloads` section with one line per entry — `- <title> (<severity>, <anchor>)
— <reason>: triaged as <real defect → counted under the matching heading | not a defect → why>`.
`verdict-derive.sh` reads the sibling envelope (`adversarial-<gate>.json`, or `--envelope <path>`)
and marks the trailer INCONSISTENT (exit 1) when the section is missing. Reading a sidecar row:
`payload` is the model's finding as normalised, `reject_reason` the clause it failed, and
`repair_attempted` / `repair_succeeded` whether the bounded repair round-trip ran.

**Round-1 hardening (sprint-248 review, sixteen live two-voice runs).** One list, by envelope field; both skills' copies of
this block are kept byte-identical (CMP-138 fails on any drift).

- **Two voices, one envelope.** The companion runs in its own sub-workdir with a log and its own copies of the prompt files.
  The envelope's `cost_usd` / tokens are BOTH voices; the per-voice spend stays under `companion_voice.cost_cents`, and
  `budget_cents` is a per-voice cap (a malformed cap is 0 cents — the run fails closed with `status: budget_exceeded`).
  Findings carry `voice` (the outer hop, matching `final_model`) and `answered_by` (the model that produced them);
  `companion_voice.answered_by` is the companion's own succeeded id. An operator may set
  `flatline_protocol.<block>.companion_chain: {anthropic: [...], openai: [...]}` to replace the default chains of D-2.1
  (used as given; only those two keys are read — keyed by the companion's family). A family with neither a credential nor its CLI on PATH is `reason: no_route`; a prompt copy that fails
  is `reason: prompt_copy_failed` (no fork). `LOA_ADVERSARIAL_KEEP_WORKDIR=1` keeps the `/tmp` workdir's files, never a
  process.
- **`companion_voice.independent` / `counted_as`.** Independence compares the two `answered_by` families (the primary's
  succeeded id, not its configured hop). Same family — or either family `unknown`, an id no catalog entry or name rule
  places, which is no evidence of a second family: the companion's findings are kept (tagged) but its envelope
  contributes no voice to verdict quality — `counted_as: duplicate_voice` (the aggregator counts distinct voices; its
  INV-5 forbids one id both succeeded and dropped, so a failed companion whose id is one of the primary's succeeded voices
  feeds no dropped-voice envelope either, and a MIXED attempt envelope keeps its own voice: a copy without the conflicting
  dropped entry is aggregated — `primary_attempts_rewritten` / `companion_attempts_rewritten`; an envelope with no
  succeeded voice that dropped the other side's voice is excluded — `primary_attempts_excluded` /
  `companion_attempts_excluded`). A primary that never answered leaves the companion `counted_as: sole_voice`
  (`independent: null`). A primary chain that exhausts while the companion completes is promoted (`status: reviewed`,
  `degraded: true`, `primary_voice: {status: failed}`) so the completed voice is never buried. An aggregator failure is
  named on the envelope (`verdict_quality_error`). A fold that fails keeps the primary envelope
  (`companion_voice.status: fold_failed`) and counts the companion as a dropped voice.
- **Shared hops (`companion_voice.shared_hops`, `primary_voice.status: ceded`).** A hop both chains hold (typically the
  other family's CLI as the primary's last resort) stays in the companion chain and is listed under `shared_hops`,
  compared by canonical name (a provider prefix or a catalog alias is the same hop). When the primary reaches a shared hop
  it waits for the companion to settle (bounded by the wait cap) and skips the hop only when the companion ANSWERED with
  it — `model_attempts` records `<hop>:skipped_shared_with_companion` and the envelope says `primary_voice: {status:
  ceded, hop}` with `degraded: false`; a companion that failed the hop, or never reached it, leaves it to the primary; a
  companion still ON the hop past the wait cap is reaped where the primary stands and the primary runs the hop; a
  companion that already answered and is finishing (its post phase) is left to the post budget. The binary is never run
  twice for the same prompt.
- **Rejected rows (`metadata.rejected_summary`, `metadata.rejected_sidecars`).** Every rejected payload lands in a sidecar
  row and in `rejected_summary` (each entry carries the row's `index` and the raw payload's title —
  `title_derived` when only the normaliser's positional id names it; an empty id or title is absent); the companion's
  rows are in its own `-companion.jsonl`, named on the envelope (`companion_voice.rejected_sidecar`, `null` and the file
  removed when nothing was rejected). `verdict-derive.sh` counts the rows of the sidecars the envelope names
  (`rejected_sidecars`): at start the run moves the previous run's envelope and its two sidecars aside (`.prev`) and it
  lists the sidecars it produced; a run that writes its envelope drops the `.prev` files; a run that aborts leaves NO envelope
  at the path and the `.prev` files beside it (the previous round's evidence, already triaged in that round's feedback);
  `LOA_ADVERSARIAL_RUN_TAG` scopes the NAMES — `adversarial-rejected-<gate>[-companion][-<tag>].jsonl` — so a chunk driver
  passes its chunk key and nothing is renamed afterwards (a tag outside `[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}` becomes a short hash of its
  raw value, said once, so distinct tags never share a file). A non-empty sidecar a listing envelope does not name is never
  silent whatever its age: its rows count toward the section and a warning names the file (newer than the envelope: the
  envelope may be stale — re-run; older: an earlier run's rows that were never folded — triage them or remove the file; a
  chunk driver clears the directory's rejected set at the start of a round). Without an envelope, or without that field,
  every `adversarial-rejected-<gate>*.jsonl` beside the envelope's place counts. A pre-FR-2 envelope (no metadata at all,
  or a metadata without a `rejected_summary` key and without any FR-2 marker — `rejected_sidecars`, `companion_voice`;
  never `rejected_count`, which the writer before cycle-126 set too) counts none of the rows as old as itself, with a
  warning — historical sprints keep their verdicts — but a sidecar NEWER than it counts (one git tracks with its committed
  bytes is history, whatever mtime a checkout gave it). Rows whose repair succeeded
  never count; a trailer-less file is held to the contract too; the same section with one top-level bullet per payload
  clears it in every case.
- **Wait cap and reaping (`failure_class: timeout`).** The second voice is reaped on INT/TERM/EXIT (one cleanup trap for
  the whole run, the whole process tree — re-collected after the freeze and before KILL — TERM then KILL after
  `LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REAP_GRACE_SECONDS`, the companion's pid trusted only while its start token matches the one recorded at
  the fork) and by a wait cap measured from its start: each `*-headless` hop counts the CLI adapter's bound — connect +
  max(600 s, the catalog's per-model `headless_timeout_seconds`, CLI hops only, capped at 3,600 s when the catalog loads;
  `claude-headless` carries 900 s because a dissent on `claude -p` takes 6–10 minutes; `LOA_ADVERSARIAL_CLI_HOP_TIMEOUT` is
  the fallback for a hop no catalog lists; a listed hop without the key is bound by the formula, 610 s) — each HTTP hop `timeout_seconds`, plus its lock wait and the CLI bound when its catalog chain falls through to a CLI
  hop (it takes that binary's lock before its request, as a `queue` phase; cheval walks the chain inside one call), plus
  30 s (`LOA_ADVERSARIAL_COMPANION_WAIT_SECONDS` pins it). The deadline follows the companion's phase (queue → hop → post) under a global ceiling; the post-hop work
  (validation, repair round-trips) has its own budget, so a model that answered is never reaped mid-processing; the
  primary's wait on a shared hop applies the same model (a companion in `post` on another hop frees the hop at once; on
  the shared hop the primary waits for the settled record). The previous run's envelope and sidecars are moved aside at
  start (`.prev`) and never restored — see "Rejected rows". Every
  numeric knob (`timeout_seconds`, the context-escalation sizes, the operator seconds) is a whole number
  without a leading zero, or its default applies with a warning — except `budget_cents` / `--budget`, which fail closed
  (0 cents, `status: budget_exceeded`, exit 4).
- **Locks.** `*-headless` hops — the dissent hops, the repair round-trips, and an HTTP alias whose catalog chain falls
  through to a CLI hop — are serialised per CLI binary across the two walks (a per-user flock under
  `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`/`$TMPDIR`, 0700, ours, never a symlink); a lock not acquired within the hop's bound fails that hop as
  `lock_wait` — no request was sent (the chain walks on); a model that merely resolves to a CLI hop, and a repair, wait only their own call
  timeout; queueing for the lock is not charged to the hop's cap; without `flock` (or a lock directory that is not ours)
  the serialisation is off and said once per run. The queue is one hop deep by design: a chunk driver runs dissents
  sequentially when any chain holds a `*-headless` hop. The envelope `adversarial-<gate>.json` and the two sidecars are
  single-writer per (sprint, gate) — the tag scopes the sidecar names only, never the envelope — so a second live run for
  the same sprint and gate is refused before it removes anything (`status: refused_concurrent_run` under `--json`; a
  dead run's lock is taken over; the token is the acquiring pid and its start time; a lock directory with no token yet is a
  holder in flight for `LOA_ADVERSARIAL_RUN_LOCK_GRACE_SECONDS`, default 5). A diff that prepares to no content is refused
  before the run lock (`status: nothing_to_review` under `--json`, exit 1, no call made); a top-priority file not even one
  hunk of which fits the budget is sent as its PARTIAL marker alone (`0 of N hunks shown`).
- **`failure_class` and `last_error`.** The class follows cheval's exit codes — 4 (`MISSING_API_KEY`) `auth`; 6
  (`BUDGET_EXCEEDED` / `RATE_LIMITED`) or a diagnostic saying "rate limit" / "429" / "quota" `quota`; 3 / 124 `timeout`,
  and a diagnostic saying "timed out" (cheval reports its own CLI-hop timeout as `PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE`) too; 5
  (`INVALID_RESPONSE`) or a `malformed_response` status `malformed`; anything else (1: API error, provider unavailable,
  token revoked) `model_unavailable`; a hop whose CLI lock was never acquired is `lock_wait` (no request was sent).
  `last_error` is an allowlisted summary of the provider's own line — cheval's error
  tokens, "timed out after Ns", HTTP / exit codes — read from the MODELINV ledger row cheval wrote for the call (the
  model-adapter shim discards cheval's stderr; the row is matched by model, primitive and the window of the companion's
  LAST hop, so a repair on the same model during its post phase is not its row; concurrent dissents on one host could still
  supply each other's line — another reason drivers run sequentially), else from the last non-banner line of the
  companion's log; it also masks bare provider-key shapes (`sk-…`, `xai-…`, `gsk_…`, `AIza…`) the shared redactor does not
  cover. The redacted raw line is printed to stderr and stays in the `/tmp` workdir, removed on exit; the a2a directory
  receives the envelope and the sidecars.
- **Repairs (`repair_hops_skipped`, `repair_budget_exhausted`).** The repair round-trip walks `tiny` (with an Anthropic
  credential) → `claude-headless` (with the binary on PATH) → the voice that answered, always last, one bounded attempt
  each (by canonical name: a prefixed answering voice is not appended twice); a hop that failed with an explicit auth /
  quota code is retired for the run's remaining repairs, the answering voice never; a repair skips a hop the companion is
  running at that moment (`repair_hops_skipped` names it, once) and waits for a CLI lock only its own timeout (a hop
  whose wait expires never ran: named `<hop>:lock_wait`, once, and no repair slot is spent); the run's
  repairs share a wall-clock budget (`LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REPAIR_BUDGET_SECONDS`, default 5 × timeout × 2 or twice the heaviest hop's charge
  (below) plus a timeout if that is more; a hop whose estimate — twice its last observed duration, at least the timeout,
  at most its bound — exceeds what is left is not started and is named `<hop>:over_budget`; spent, the rest are rejected
  unrepaired and counted in `repair_budget_exhausted`, a payload none of whose hops started for want of budget among them;
  one none of whose hops started for any other reason — every hop retired or being run by the companion — is counted in
  `repair_skipped_no_hop`). `LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REPAIR_MODEL` is filtered by the retired hops too. A hop is charged by what it
  can reach, in the repair budget and the companion's post budget alike: a `*-headless` hop its CLI bound, an HTTP alias
  whose chain falls through to a CLI its lock wait, its timeout and that CLI's bound. A derived
  finding id never collides with one the model supplied; the normaliser's `id_derived` / `failure_mode_derived` markers are
  not part of the repair's byte-diff; a derived `failure_mode` shorter than 20 characters (an enumerator, an abbreviation)

  INV-5 forbids one id both succeeded and dropped, so a failed companion whose id is one of the primary's succeeded voices
  feeds no dropped-voice envelope either, and a MIXED attempt envelope keeps its own voice: a copy without the conflicting
  dropped entry is aggregated — `primary_attempts_rewritten` / `companion_attempts_rewritten`; an envelope with no
  succeeded voice that dropped the other side's voice is excluded — `primary_attempts_excluded` /
  `companion_attempts_excluded`). A primary that never answered leaves the companion `counted_as: sole_voice`
  (`independent: null`). A primary chain that exhausts while the companion completes is promoted (`status: reviewed`,
  `degraded: true`, `primary_voice: {status: failed}`) so the completed voice is never buried. An aggregator failure is
  named on the envelope (`verdict_quality_error`). A fold that fails keeps the primary envelope
  (`companion_voice.status: fold_failed`) and counts the companion as a dropped voice.
- **Shared hops (`companion_voice.shared_hops`, `primary_voice.status: ceded`).** A hop both chains hold (typically the
  other family's CLI as the primary's last resort) stays in the companion chain and is listed under `shared_hops`,
  compared by canonical name (a provider prefix or a catalog alias is the same hop). When the primary reaches a shared hop
  it waits for the companion to settle (bounded by the wait cap) and skips the hop only when the companion ANSWERED with
  it — `model_attempts` records `<hop>:skipped_shared_with_companion` and the envelope says `primary_voice: {status:
  ceded, hop}` with `degraded: false`; a companion that failed the hop, or never reached it, leaves it to the primary; a
  companion still ON the hop past the wait cap is reaped where the primary stands and the primary runs the hop; a
  companion that already answered and is finishing (its post phase) is left to the post budget. The binary is never run
  twice for the same prompt.
- **Rejected rows (`metadata.rejected_summary`, `metadata.rejected_sidecars`).** Every rejected payload lands in a sidecar
  row and in `rejected_summary` (each entry carries the row's `index` and the raw payload's title —
  `title_derived` when only the normaliser's positional id names it; an empty id or title is absent); the companion's
  rows are in its own `-companion.jsonl`, named on the envelope (`companion_voice.rejected_sidecar`, `null` and the file
  removed when nothing was rejected). `verdict-derive.sh` counts the rows of the sidecars the envelope names
  (`rejected_sidecars`): at start the run moves the previous run's envelope and its two sidecars aside (`.prev`) and it
  lists the sidecars it produced; a run that writes its envelope drops the `.prev` files; a run that aborts leaves NO envelope
  at the path and the `.prev` files beside it (the previous round's evidence, already triaged in that round's feedback);
  `LOA_ADVERSARIAL_RUN_TAG` scopes the NAMES — `adversarial-rejected-<gate>[-companion][-<tag>].jsonl` — so a chunk driver
  passes its chunk key and nothing is renamed afterwards (a tag outside `[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}` becomes a short hash of its
  raw value, said once, so distinct tags never share a file). A non-empty sidecar a listing envelope does not name is never
  silent whatever its age: its rows count toward the section and a warning names the file (newer than the envelope: the
  envelope may be stale — re-run; older: an earlier run's rows that were never folded — triage them or remove the file; a
  chunk driver clears the directory's rejected set at the start of a round). Without an envelope, or without that field,
  every `adversarial-rejected-<gate>*.jsonl` beside the envelope's place counts. A pre-FR-2 envelope (no metadata at all,
  or a metadata without a `rejected_summary` key and without any FR-2 marker — `rejected_sidecars`, `companion_voice`;
  never `rejected_count`, which the writer before cycle-126 set too) counts none of the rows as old as itself, with a
  warning — historical sprints keep their verdicts — but a sidecar NEWER than it counts (one git tracks with its committed
  bytes is history, whatever mtime a checkout gave it). Rows whose repair succeeded
  never count; a trailer-less file is held to the contract too; the same section with one top-level bullet per payload
  clears it in every case.
- **Wait cap and reaping (`failure_class: timeout`).** The second voice is reaped on INT/TERM/EXIT (one cleanup trap for
  the whole run, the whole process tree — re-collected after the freeze and before KILL — TERM then KILL after
  `LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REAP_GRACE_SECONDS`, the companion's pid trusted only while its start token matches the one recorded at
  the fork) and by a wait cap measured from its start: each `*-headless` hop counts the CLI adapter's bound — connect +
  max(600 s, the catalog's per-model `headless_timeout_seconds`, CLI hops only, capped at 3,600 s when the catalog loads;
  `claude-headless` carries 900 s because a dissent on `claude -p` takes 6–10 minutes; `LOA_ADVERSARIAL_CLI_HOP_TIMEOUT` is
  the fallback for a hop no catalog lists; a listed hop without the key is bound by the formula, 610 s) — each HTTP hop `timeout_seconds`, plus its lock wait and the CLI bound when its catalog chain falls through to a CLI
  hop (it takes that binary's lock before its request, as a `queue` phase; cheval walks the chain inside one call), plus
  30 s (`LOA_ADVERSARIAL_COMPANION_WAIT_SECONDS` pins it). The deadline follows the companion's phase (queue → hop → post) under a global ceiling; the post-hop work
  (validation, repair round-trips) has its own budget, so a model that answered is never reaped mid-processing; the
  primary's wait on a shared hop applies the same model (a companion in `post` on another hop frees the hop at once; on
  the shared hop the primary waits for the settled record). The previous run's envelope and sidecars are moved aside at
  start (`.prev`) and never restored — see "Rejected rows". Every
  numeric knob (`timeout_seconds`, the context-escalation sizes, the operator seconds) is a whole number
  without a leading zero, or its default applies with a warning — except `budget_cents` / `--budget`, which fail closed
  (0 cents, `status: budget_exceeded`, exit 4).
- **Locks.** `*-headless` hops — the dissent hops, the repair round-trips, and an HTTP alias whose catalog chain falls
  through to a CLI hop — are serialised per CLI binary across the two walks (a per-user flock under
  `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`/`$TMPDIR`, 0700, ours, never a symlink); a lock not acquired within the hop's bound fails that hop as
  `lock_wait` — no request was sent (the chain walks on); a model that merely resolves to a CLI hop, and a repair, wait only their own call
  timeout; queueing for the lock is not charged to the hop's cap; without `flock` (or a lock directory that is not ours)
  the serialisation is off and said once per run. The queue is one hop deep by design: a chunk driver runs dissents
  sequentially when any chain holds a `*-headless` hop. The envelope `adversarial-<gate>.json` and the two sidecars are
  single-writer per (sprint, gate) — the tag scopes the sidecar names only, never the envelope — so a second live run for
  the same sprint and gate is refused before it removes anything (`status: refused_concurrent_run` under `--json`; a
  dead run's lock is taken over; the token is the acquiring pid and its start time; a lock directory with no token yet is a
  holder in flight for `LOA_ADVERSARIAL_RUN_LOCK_GRACE_SECONDS`, default 5). A diff that prepares to no content is refused
  before the run lock (`status: nothing_to_review` under `--json`, exit 1, no call made); a top-priority file not even one
  hunk of which fits the budget is sent as its PARTIAL marker alone (`0 of N hunks shown`).
- **`failure_class` and `last_error`.** The class follows cheval's exit codes — 4 (`MISSING_API_KEY`) `auth`; 6
  (`BUDGET_EXCEEDED` / `RATE_LIMITED`) or a diagnostic saying "rate limit" / "429" / "quota" `quota`; 3 / 124 `timeout`,
  and a diagnostic saying "timed out" (cheval reports its own CLI-hop timeout as `PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE`) too; 5
  (`INVALID_RESPONSE`) or a `malformed_response` status `malformed`; anything else (1: API error, provider unavailable,
  token revoked) `model_unavailable`; a hop whose CLI lock was never acquired is `lock_wait` (no request was sent).
  `last_error` is an allowlisted summary of the provider's own line — cheval's error
  tokens, "timed out after Ns", HTTP / exit codes — read from the MODELINV ledger row cheval wrote for the call (the
  model-adapter shim discards cheval's stderr; the row is matched by model, primitive and the window of the companion's
  LAST hop, so a repair on the same model during its post phase is not its row; concurrent dissents on one host could still
  supply each other's line — another reason drivers run sequentially), else from the last non-banner line of the
  companion's log; it also masks bare provider-key shapes (`sk-…`, `xai-…`, `gsk_…`, `AIza…`) the shared redactor does not
  cover. The redacted raw line is printed to stderr and stays in the `/tmp` workdir, removed on exit; the a2a directory
  receives the envelope and the sidecars.
- **Repairs (`repair_hops_skipped`, `repair_budget_exhausted`).** The repair round-trip walks `tiny` (with an Anthropic
  credential) → `claude-headless` (with the binary on PATH) → the voice that answered, always last, one bounded attempt
  each (by canonical name: a prefixed answering voice is not appended twice); a hop that failed with an explicit auth /
  quota code is retired for the run's remaining repairs, the answering voice never; a repair skips a hop the companion is
  running at that moment (`repair_hops_skipped` names it, once) and waits for a CLI lock only its own timeout (a hop
  whose wait expires never ran: named `<hop>:lock_wait`, once, and no repair slot is spent); the run's
  repairs share a wall-clock budget (`LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REPAIR_BUDGET_SECONDS`, default 5 × timeout × 2 or twice the heaviest hop's charge
  (below) plus a timeout if that is more; a hop whose estimate — twice its last observed duration, at least the timeout,
  at most its bound — exceeds what is left is not started and is named `<hop>:over_budget`; spent, the rest are rejected
  unrepaired and counted in `repair_budget_exhausted`, a payload none of whose hops started for want of budget among them;
  one none of whose hops started for any other reason — every hop retired or being run by the companion — is counted in
  `repair_skipped_no_hop`). `LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REPAIR_MODEL` is filtered by the retired hops too. A hop is charged by what it
  can reach, in the repair budget and the companion's post budget alike: a `*-headless` hop its CLI bound, an HTTP alias
  whose chain falls through to a CLI its lock wait, its timeout and that CLI's bound. A derived
  finding id never collides with one the model supplied; the normaliser's `id_derived` / `failure_mode_derived` markers are
  not part of the repair's byte-diff; a derived `failure_mode` shorter than 20 characters (an enumerator, an abbreviation)

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# =============================================================================
3	# loa-kf-surface.sh — SessionStart hook (cycle-115 sprint-1, D1).
4	#
5	# Surfaces a compact symptom -> KF table from grimoires/loa/known-failures.md
6	# at session start so an agent sees the operational-failure log before
7	# triaging. DEFAULT-OFF: gated on `known_failures.surface_at_session_start`
8	# (default false) in .loa.config.yaml.
9	#
10	# STREAM ROUTING: Claude Code's SessionStart contract injects a hook's STDOUT
11	#   (on exit 0) into the session as context; STDERR is transcript-only and never
12	#   reaches the agent. This surface is only useful IN CONTEXT, so every ENABLED
13	#   path — the healthy table AND the enabled-but-degraded WARNINGs — writes to
14	#   STDOUT (an agent under the index-first intake contract must SEE that the KF
15	#   surface is degraded so it falls back to regenerating the index). Sibling
16	#   surfacing hooks (loa-l6-surface-handoffs.sh, loa-l7-surface-soul.sh) route
17	#   the same way. The DISABLED path emits nothing at all.
18	#
19	# CONTRACT (loud-but-nonblocking — this is OBSERVABILITY, never a gate):
20	#   - It MUST exit 0 in ALL paths. It MUST NOT block a session.
21	#   - When the flag is DISABLED (or config/yq absent): emit NOTHING, exit 0.
22	#   - When ENABLED but the surface is degraded — known-failures.md unreadable,
23	#     or zero KF entries parsed — emit a visible "[KF-SURFACE] WARNING ..."
24	#     to STDOUT and exit 0 (loud + in-context, so the agent notices a broken
25	#     knowledge surface; never silent on an enabled-but-broken path).
26	#   - When ENABLED and healthy: emit a compact symptom -> KF table to STDOUT,
27	#     exit 0.
28	#
29	# TRUST BOUNDARY: known-failures.md bodies are UNTRUSTED at surfacing. Every
30	#   field is control-byte-sanitized + length-capped before reaching session
31	#   context; body prose is NEVER interpreted as instructions (CLAUDE.md
32	#   agent-network universal invariant).
33	# =============================================================================
34	set -uo pipefail
35	
36	HOOK_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
37	REPO_ROOT="$(cd "${HOOK_DIR}/../.." && pwd)"
38	
39	# --- test-mode seam (mirrors L4/L6/L7 cycle-098 gate): the config + path
40	#     overrides are honored ONLY under LOA_KF_SURFACE_TEST_MODE=1 with a bats
41	#     marker present. In production neither override is consulted. -----------
42	_kf_test_mode_active() {
43	  [[ "${LOA_KF_SURFACE_TEST_MODE:-0}" == "1" ]] || return 1
44	  [[ -n "${BATS_TEST_FILENAME:-}" ]] && return 0
45	  [[ -n "${BATS_VERSION:-}" ]] && return 0
46	  return 1
47	}
48	
49	# Sanitize: drop control bytes (keep UTF-8 multibyte), flatten whitespace, cap.
50	_san() { printf '%s' "${1-}" | tr -d '\000-\010\013\014\016-\037\177' | tr '\t\n\r' '   ' | sed -E 's/  +/ /g; s/^ //; s/ $//' | cut -c1-100; }
51	
52	# --- resolve enabled flag -----------------------------------------------------
53	enabled="false"
54	if _kf_test_mode_active && [[ -n "${LOA_KF_SURFACE_TEST_CONFIG-}" ]]; then
55	  # In test mode the override stands in for the parsed config value.
56	  enabled="${LOA_KF_SURFACE_TEST_CONFIG}"
57	else
58	  config_path="${REPO_ROOT}/.loa.config.yaml"
59	  # No yq or no config -> the feature is opt-in and unconfigurable here: silent.
60	  if command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1 && [[ -f "$config_path" ]]; then
61	    # Explicit key, else the loa.profile default (cycle-129 D-9.1).
62	    # shellcheck source=scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh
63	    source "${REPO_ROOT}/.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh" 2>/dev/null &&
64	      enabled="$(loa_knob known_failures.surface_at_session_start false 2>/dev/null || echo false)"
65	  fi
66	fi
67	
68	# DISABLED (or unconfigurable) -> emit nothing, exit 0. This is the ONLY silent path.
69	[[ "$enabled" == "true" ]] || exit 0
70	
71	# --- ENABLED: from here every exit is loud-or-table, always exit 0 -----------

Perfect. Now I have enough information to find defects. Let me analyze systematically:

## Key findings:

Based on my review, here are the concrete defects I found:

### 1. **Race condition in atomic_update with derived_at timing** 
- **File**: `/workspace/pr/head/.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh:459-463`
- **Issue**: When `cmd_derive` calls `atomic_update` to write `.state`, `.status`, `.derived_at`, and `.derivation` fields, there's a window where `.derived_at` is written AFTER the breaker file is updated. If a concurrent read in `implement-gate.sh` checks the sprint-plan-state.json between the breaker write (line 456) and the sprint-plan-state write (line 459), it will see either the old `.derived_at` or find `.derived_at` missing, causing `read_position` (line 558 in implement-gate.sh) to fail with "cache not derived" when it should succeed.
- **Confidence**: HIGH

### 2. **Missing null check on `jq -r '.derived_at // empty | strings'` in `_ig_derived_ok`**
- **File**: `/workspace/pr/head/.claude/hooks/compliance/implement-gate.sh:501-503`
- **Issue**: Line 502 does `[[ -z "$da" ]] && return 0`, which returns success (0) when `derived_at` is absent. This means a cache WITHOUT `derived_at` is treated as VALID for sanction purposes in `check_implementation_active` (line 510). However, `read_position` (line 553 onwards) requires `derived_at` to be present and recent to determine the run position. This inconsistency means an old-schema file without `derived_at` can be sanctioned in `check_implementation_active` but then fail to resolve position in `read_position`, creating an edge case.
- **Exact Code**: Line 502 returns 0 (success) when `$da` is empty. But callers expect this to validate recency.
- **Scenario**: A file written by the old code (base version, no `derived_at`) gets sanctioned by `check_implementation_active`, but then `deny` mode cannot read its position (line 554 check fails).
- **Confidence**: HIGH

### 3. **Incorrect jq filter for sanitizing derived values in karpathy-surgical-diff-check.sh**
- **File**: `/workspace/pr/head/.claude/hooks/quality/karpathy-surgical-diff-check.sh:1348`
- **Issue**: The checkpoint read uses `gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9._-]"; "_")` but the `_sanitise` function later (line 1334-1339) uses `tr -c 'A-Za-z0-9._-' '_'`. These produce different results for leading dots: `gsub` leaves a dot that starts a string alone, but then `_sanitise` catches it on line 1337. However, if the jq `gsub` result is something like `.task_name`, the second pass through `_sanitise` will convert it to `_task_name`. The inconsistency is minor but the logic doesn't match the spec at line 1335.
- **Confidence**: LOW (cosmetic, but inconsistent behavior)

### 4. **Missing quote around `$gate_mode` in `log_gate_row` call at line 408**
- **File**: `/workspace/pr/head/.claude/hooks/compliance/implement-gate.sh:408`
- **Issue**: Line 408 calls `log_gate_row` with `--arg mode "$gate_mode"`. If `gate_mode` is ever unset (e.g., sourcing fails), this would pass an empty string. The code sets `gate_mode="ask"` at line 328, but if `load_gate_config` is never called before line 408 (in the `--effective-mode` path), it will use the default. However, this is mitigated by the explicit initialization at line 328.
- **Confidence**: LOW (mitigation present)

### 5. **Stale-hours boundary calculation assumes 24-hour clock safety but jq fromdateiso8601 does not handle leap seconds**
- **File**: `/workspace/pr/head/.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh:275` and implement-gate.sh:493-495
- **Issue**: The function `_ig_within` (line 493-495) and the epoch function in run-checkpoint.sh (line 274) use `jq's fromdateiso8601` which per ISO-8601 does NOT handle leap seconds. If a timestamp includes a `60` second (leap second), `fromdateiso8601` will silently truncate or fail. On hosts with leap-second-aware systems, this could cause timestamps with leap seconds to parse as null, making `_ig_within` return 1 (false), falsely marking a fresh cache as stale.
- **Scenario**: A timestamp "2026-06-30T23:59:60Z" (leap second) won't parse correctly in jq.
- **Confidence**: MEDIUM (rare, but possible)

### 6. **Empty jq --argjson string without validation in `log_gate_row`**
- **File**: `/workspace/pr/head/.claude/hooks/compliance/implement-gate.sh:401-410`
- **Issue**: At line 401, `_ig_replay_json='{"replay":true}'` is set conditionally, but at line 410 it's passed to `jq ... --argjson replay "$_ig_replay_json"`. If `_ig_replay_json` is set to `'{}'` (line 357), this is valid JSON. However, the code never validates that `_ig_replay_json` is valid JSON before passing it to `--argjson`. If the initialization at line 357 or line 358 were ever corrupted, `jq --argjson` would fail with exit 5, and the append would be silently dropped (line 410 `|| true`).
- **Confidence**: LOW (hardcoded values, but violation of the general principle from shell-conventions.md)

### 7. **Log row skips essential fields when claims modifier logs a deny**
- **File**: `/workspace/pr/head/.claude/hooks/compliance/implement-gate.sh:440`
- **Issue**: When a non-implementation claim causes a deny (line 603), `log_model_signal deny` is called which adds `hook: "implement-gate", action: $decision, gate_mode: $gmode` to the row (line 440). But this row ALSO gets its own `hook: "implement-gate"` and `action: "deny"` in `emit_deny` output context. The audit.jsonl will have TWO overlapping fields for the same event, which could confuse downstream consumers.
- **Scenario**: A row from `log_model_signal deny` at line 440 sets `hook` and `action`, but they're not the same format as a row from `log_gate_row deny deny` at line 631.
- **Confidence**: MEDIUM (inconsistent audit trail format)

### 8. **Missing handling of unparseable derived_at in runtime position resolution**
- **File**: `/workspace/pr/head/.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh:387-394`
- **Issue**: When computing `commit_after_verdict` (line 393), the code tries to parse verdict timestamps with `sub("\\.[0-9]+Z$"; "Z") | try fromdateiso8601 catch 0`. If either `$vts` (verdict timestamps) or `$c[1]` (commit epoch) fail to parse, they'll be null/0. If both are null, the line produces `null` instead of `false`. But the field is used as a boolean in downstream logic (implied by field name). Consumers might treat `null` as falsy, but the contract is unclear.
- **Confidence**: MEDIUM (implicit contract, behavior depends on downstream)

### 9. **Marker lifecycle: "implement-active.json" not synced in derived_at window**
- **File**: `/workspace/pr/head/.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh` and implement-gate.sh
- **Issue**: The `run-checkpoint.sh mark` command (lines 534-545) writes `implement-active.json` and then calls `cmd_derive --write` (line 541). However, if `cmd_derive` fails (drc != 0 and drc != 4, line 542), the marker is still present but the cache is not updated. Meanwhile, `implement-gate.sh` checks the marker BEFORE deriving the position (line 583-590). This creates a window where an stale marker can sanction a write when the derived cache would deny it.
- **Scenario**: `mark` is called, marker is written, `derive --write` is skipped or fails, then a gate check sees the fresh marker and allows a write that should be denied based on the actual run state.
- **Confidence**: MEDIUM

### 10. **Profile-lib.sh seam uses LOA_STATUS_CONFIG_FILE but loa-status.sh environment is not portable**
- **File**: `/workspace/pr/head/.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh:2898-2902`
- **Issue**: Line 2898-2901 honor `LOA_STATUS_CONFIG_FILE` only when running under bats (`BATS_TEST_FILENAME` or `BATS_VERSION` is set). However, in test RCD-R5 (line 6693 in the diff), the test sets `LOA_STATUS_CONFIG_FILE` without setting `BATS_TEST_FILENAME`. This means the seam will NOT be honored, and the config will fall back to the default, causing the test to read the wrong config. The test will still pass if the error happens to align, but the seam is ineffective.
- **Confidence**: MEDIUM

---

## Verified as Correct:

1. **`atomic_update` pattern with flock**: The double-validation (jq on original file, then jq -e on temp) before mv is correct and prevents partial writes.
2. **Exit codes**: `cmd_derive` returns 0 on success, 4 on no ledger (acceptable skip), 2 on usage, 3 on write failure. Consistent.
3. **Checkpoint discard logic**: Correctly discards closed-bead verification on `br` unavailability (return 2) as distinct from closed (0) vs. open (1).
4. **Stale marker detection**: The `stale_marker` flag correctly detects when COMPLETED marker names a different sprint via the trailer or sprint: line.

---

## Findings Summary:

**head/.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh:459-463** — race condition between breaker and sprint-plan-state writes in `cmd_derive --write`; `derived_at` is not yet written when concurrent implement-gate reads

**head/.claude/hooks/compliance/implement-gate.sh:502** — `_ig_derived_ok` returns success (0) when `derived_at` is absent, but `read_position` requires it present, creating inconsistent contract

**head/.claude/hooks/compliance/implement-gate.sh:440** — non-implementation claim deny rows mix log_model_signal and log_gate_row formats, creating inconsistent audit.jsonl structure

**head/.claude/hooks/compliance/implement-gate.sh:583-590** — marker sanction check is not re-derived when `cmd_derive` fails in `mark` subcommand (line 541-542), creating window for stale marker to sanction

**head/.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh:2898-2901** — `LOA_STATUS_CONFIG_FILE` seam only honored under bats, but test RCD-R5 (line 6693) sets it without bats markers, so seam is ineffective

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# =============================================================================
3	# run-checkpoint.sh — run position in .run/ (cycle-125 FR-3, SDD D-3.2;
4	# cycle-129 FR-4(f)/FR-5, SDD D-4.6, D-5.1 … D-5.4). Beads are the task ledger;
5	# the checkpoint is a HINT; the run state and the breaker are caches DERIVED
6	# from files (COMPLETED markers, LOA-VERDICT trailers, the ledger, git).
7	#
8	#   run-checkpoint.sh write --sprint sprint-N --phase PHASE [--task BEAD-ID] [--file F]
9	#       Atomically sets .schema_version = 2, .checkpoint = {sprint, task, phase, ts}
10	#       and .timestamps.last_activity = ts: jq → F.tmp.$$ → mv -f, under flock
11	#       on F.lock. F must already exist (a run in progress). Then runs
12	#       `derive --write` (a missing ledger is skipped). Exit 0 · 2 usage /
13	#       no run · 3 write failed (the previous file is untouched).
14	#   run-checkpoint.sh read [--file F] [--json]
15	#       Prints the checkpoint when it is trustworthy: parses, and when a task
16	#       is named, `br show <task> --json` reports it closed (a checkpoint that
17	#       names an open or unknown bead is DISCARDED with a logged line — beads
18	#       remain the recovery source). schema_version 1 / no checkpoint → prints
19	#       "sprint granularity". Exit 0 always when F exists; 2 when it does not.
20	#   run-checkpoint.sh derive [--json] [--write] [--root DIR] [--file F]
21	#       For the ledger's active cycle, per sprint: global_id, local_label,
22	#       ledger status, completed_marker (a2a/sprint-<gid>/COMPLETED exists and
23	#       the feedback trailers name this sprint, as sprint-<gid> or the local
24	#       label; a trailer or a `sprint:` line naming another sprint makes it a
25	#       stale_marker, treated as absent), review/audit verdicts (verdict-derive.sh;
26	#       APPROVED needs exit 0; a file without a trailer is legacy: no verdict,
27	#       listed in derivation.legacy_feedback), impl_commit (newest non-merge
28	#       commit on HEAD since max(sprint started|created, cycle created) touching
29	#       a path outside grimoires/, .run/, REPO-MAP.md, checksums.json,
30	#       CHANGELOG.md) and state complete | awaiting_marker | in_progress.
31	#       Run state, first match wins:
32	#         cache .state or .status JACKED_OUT, or .completion.merged_sha → JACKED_OUT (terminal)
33	#         breaker OPEN, or cache HALTED                                 → HALTED (sticky until /run-resume)
34	#         every sprint complete                                         → COMPLETE
35	#         cache COMPLETE and the ledger registers no new incomplete sprint → COMPLETE
36	#         last_activity within run_mode.stale_hours (12)                → RUNNING
37	#         otherwise                                                     → INTERRUPTED
38	#       Breaker (active sprint = first incomplete, else the last): the ordered
39	#       rounds engineer-feedback-r*.md, auditor-sprint-feedback-r*.md and the
40	#       current files (sorted by trailer ts, round, gate; rounds before the
41	#       breaker's reset_at are ignored) give cycle_count (non-APPROVED rounds),
42	#       same_issue (consecutive equal hashes) and no_progress (consecutive
43	#       equal counts); each cached counter is raised to its recomputed value,
44	#       never lowered; OPEN when a count threshold is met (timeout is left to
45	#       record-round). --json prints the derivation; --write rewrites F

3	# profile-lib.sh — `loa.profile` resolution (cycle-129 SDD D-9.1, §5.3;
4	# DEC-0143, DEC-0152, DEC-0166).
5	#
6	# Sourced API (bash 3.2 safe; sets no shell options; every function returns 0
7	# unless stated):
8	#   loa_profile                     → lean | standard | full
9	#   loa_profile_source              → explicit | default | invalid
10	#   loa_knob <yq-path> <fallback>   → the effective value of one config key:
11	#        the key set explicitly in the config (an explicit `false` counts —
12	#        never `// default`, which reads false as absent), else the selected
13	#        profile's value when the key is a profile key, else <fallback>.
14	#        Returns 2 (printing the fallback) on a malformed path.
15	#   loa_profile_overrides           → `key=value` lines, one per explicit
16	#        profile key whose value differs from the selected profile's value
17	#   loa_effective_json              → the resolved document (below)
18	#
19	# CLI: profile-lib.sh profile | source | knob <path> <fallback> | overrides | json
20	#
21	# Inputs (each has a test seam):
22	#   config    LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE, else LOA_STATUS_CONFIG_FILE (honoured
23	#             only under bats, like loa-status.sh), else <root>/.loa.config.yaml
24	#   profiles  LOA_PROFILES_FILE, else <root>/.claude/data/profiles.yaml
25	#   floor     LOA_PROFILE_FLOOR_FILE, else <root>/.claude/data/floor.yaml
26	#   root      LOA_PROFILE_ROOT, else three directories above this file
27	#
28	# Cache: <root>/.run/effective-config.json (LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE overrides),
29	# keyed on the paths and the mtime+size of the config, profiles.yaml and
30	# floor.yaml: any edit to one of them rebuilds it on the next call, so it is
31	# built once per session in practice. When the config is a seam (not the
32	# repository's own file) and no cache seam is set, nothing is cached — a test
33	# config never overwrites the repository's cache. The warm path is one stat
34	# and one jq. The write is atomic (temp file + mv in the same directory).
35	#
36	# Safety: a profile key that names a floor key (floor.yaml `floor_keys`, `*`
37	# matches one or more characters; an ancestor of a floor key also counts) is
38	# ignored with a WARN — no profile can reach the floor. Key paths are checked
39	# against ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+(\.[A-Za-z0-9_]+)*$ before they reach a yq expression.

54	  fi

59	    status_cfg="${LOA_STATUS_CONFIG_FILE:-}"
60	  fi

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# karpathy-surgical-diff-check.sh — Karpathy principle 3 (Surgical Changes),
3	# per-task diff size (#961 K-1 / FR-1; reworked by cycle-129 D-4.3, D-4.2a,
4	# DEC-0141).
5	#
6	# PostToolUse:Write|Edit|NotebookEdit hook. Counts the lines each write adds
7	# (Write → content, Edit/NotebookEdit → new_string) and keeps a running total
8	# PER TASK:
9	#
10	#   key      the current task from `run-checkpoint.sh read --json`
11	#            (`.checkpoint.task`, else the sprint), else the session id from
12	#            the hook payload (`.session_id`, else LOA_SESSION_ID, else
13	#            <user>-<UTC date>); sanitised to ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$ (any other
14	#            byte becomes `_`, a leading dot becomes `_`, cut to 128 bytes)
15	#   state    .run/karpathy-surgical/<key>.jsonl — one small file per task, so
16	#            the total resets when the task changes; the directory keeps the
17	#            20 most recently written files and deletes older ones
18	#   summary  .run/karpathy-surgical-summary.json
19	#            {task, lines, threshold, over, updated_at}, rewritten atomically
20	#            after each counted write; the review's SURGICAL axis reads it
21	#   legacy   .run/karpathy-task-state.jsonl (the old session-long total) and
22	#            its two perf caches are deleted on the first run of this layout
23	#
24	# Over `karpathy_principles.diff_lines_per_task` (default 100) it prints the
25	# `[karpathy-surgical-warn]` stderr line and appends a trajectory event
26	# (karpathy-check.payload.schema.json). Non-blocking: always exits 0. The
27	# master switch `karpathy_principles.surgical_diff_warning` is read through
28	# loa_knob (explicit key, else the loa.profile default; `lean` turns it off).
29	#
30	# Safety (NFR-Sec-1): tool_input.content / new_string never reach state,
31	# summary or trajectory — only line counts, the file path (JSON-encoded by
32	# jq) and the sanitised key. Missing jq or yq, a missing config or a
33	# malformed payload is a silent no-op. A symlinked state directory or state
34	# file is not written through.
35	#
36	# Seams (tests): LOA_CONFIG_OVERRIDE (config), KARPATHY_STATE_DIR,
37	# KARPATHY_SUMMARY_FILE, KARPATHY_LEGACY_STATE, KARPATHY_TRAJECTORY_DIR,
38	# KARPATHY_CHECKPOINT_CMD (default .claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh, which
39	# itself honours LOA_RUN_DIR), KARPATHY_STATE_KEEP (default 20).
40	#
41	# Design note: the session-long state file grew without bound, which is what
42	# the earlier perf passes (config-token and state-aggregate caches) existed
43	# to absorb. Per-task files are small and rotated, so the hook reads them in
44	# full each time and those caches are gone.

The full grammar, both class lists and the default are stated in the block comment above `_bdb_hd_is_interp` in `block-destructive-bash.sh`. In summary:
+
+- **Grammar.** The fence sees literal command text, with CRLF folded to LF. A control character, an unreadable header, more than one heredoc on a header, a non-word or variable delimiter, or a missing terminator makes the whole command scan in full.
+- **Interpreter class.** The body is scanned exactly as before. This applies when the consumer or any pipe target is a shell, interpreter, argument-running wrapper or SQL runner, when the statement holds a substitution, group or continuation, or when an allowlisted form carries an unknown or exec-shaped flag. It also applies when the write target is executable content: a script extension, a shebang first line, `.claude/hooks/`, `.claude/settings*.json`, `.git/hooks/`, an rc or profile file, `/etc`, or a directory on `PATH`. A substitution under an unquoted delimiter, an interpreter word or a variable command word sends the body back to a full scan.

+- **Export.** Source the hook with `BDB_LIB_ONLY=1` and call `_bdb_heredoc_consumer_class <command>`, which prints `interpreter`, `nonexec` or `none`. `heredoc_nonexec <command>` exits 0 for a non-executing heredoc. A lone `$` (dollar amount, `$ENV` mention, trailing bare `$`) is now permitted inside a redacted value — so `git commit -m "saved $5 by dropping find . -exec rm -rf {} +"` correctly ALLOWs. One residual false positive is **accepted by design**:

The `$(` disqualifies the value from redaction (a regex fence cannot parse subshell contents without reintroducing the #1047 bypass), so a destructive *shape* mentioned inside that subshell body still trips FR-2 and blocks a genuinely safe commit. **Workaround**: paraphrase the destructive shape in the commit body (as the cycle-119 commits did — e.g. write "find-exec-rm" rather than the literal `find … -exec rm -rf`), or drop the `$(…)` wrapper. 502	       then .triggers.no_progress.count = ((.triggers.no_progress.count // 0) + 1)
503	       else .triggers.no_progress.count = 0 end)
504	    | .triggers.no_progress.last_counts = $c

511	        elif .triggers.cycle_count.current >= (.triggers.cycle_count.limit // $th.cycles)
512	          then ["cycle_count", "\(.triggers.cycle_count.current) changes-required rounds reached the limit \(.triggers.cycle_count.limit // $th.cycles)"]
513	        elif $start != null and ($now - $start) >= ((.triggers.timeout.limit_hours // $th.hours) * 3600)

515	        elif (.state // "CLOSED") == "OPEN" then ["open", "breaker already OPEN"]
516	        else null end ) as $trip
517	    | .last_round = {gate: $gate, sprint: (if $sprint == "" then null else $sprint end), verdict: $p.verdict, hash: $p.hash, ts: $ts}

520	      elif $trip != null then .state = "OPEN"

528	    echo "TRIPPED: $trip"
529	    return 10
530	  fi
531	  return 0
532	}

272	# Shared jq definitions: time, the breaker recompute and the run-state resolution
273	JQ_DEFS='
274	def epoch: if type == "string" then (sub("\\.[0-9]+Z$"; "Z") | try fromdateiso8601 catch null) else null end;
275	def fresh($now; $win): epoch as $t | $t != null and ($now - $t) <= $win and ($t - $now) <= 300;
276	def recompute($rounds; $reset):
277	  ($rounds
278	   | map(select($reset == null or ((.ts // "") > $reset)))
279	   | sort_by([(.ts // ""), .round, (if .gate == "review" then 0 else 1 end)])
280	   | map(select(.approved | not))) as $nr
281	  | reduce $nr[] as $r ({cycle: 0, same: 0, hash: null, np: 0, lc: null};
282	      .cycle += 1
283	      | (if $r.hash != "none" and $r.hash == .hash then .same += 1 else .same = 1 | .hash = $r.hash end)
284	      | ($r.counts | tojson) as $c
285	      | (if .lc != null and .lc == $c then .np += 1 else .np = 0 end)
286	      | .lc = $c);
287	def skeleton($th; $ts):
288	  {state: "CLOSED",
289	   triggers: {same_issue: {count: 0, threshold: $th.same, last_hash: null},
290	              no_progress: {count: 0, threshold: $th.np},
291	              cycle_count: {current: 0, limit: $th.cycles},
292	              timeout: {started: $ts, limit_hours: $th.hours}},
293	   history: []};
294	def merge_breaker($rc; $th; $ts):
295	  (if type == "object" then . else skeleton($th; $ts) end)
296	  | .triggers = (.triggers // {})
297	  | .triggers.cycle_count.current = ([(.triggers.cycle_count.current // 0), $rc.cycle] | max)
298	  | (if $rc.same > (.triggers.same_issue.count // 0)
299	     then .triggers.same_issue.count = $rc.same | .triggers.same_issue.last_hash = $rc.hash else . end)
300	  | (if $rc.np > (.triggers.no_progress.count // 0) or (.triggers.no_progress.last_counts == null and $rc.lc != null)
301	     then .triggers.no_progress.count = ([(.triggers.no_progress.count // 0), $rc.np] | max)
302	          | .triggers.no_progress.last_counts = $rc.lc else . end)
303	  | ( if (.triggers.same_issue.count // 0) >= (.triggers.same_issue.threshold // $th.same)
304	        then ["same_issue", "same issue hash repeated \(.triggers.same_issue.count) times (derived from the feedback history)"]
305	      elif (.triggers.no_progress.count // 0) >= (.triggers.no_progress.threshold // $th.np)
306	        then ["no_progress", "counts unchanged for \(.triggers.no_progress.count) consecutive rounds (derived from the feedback history)"]
307	      elif (.triggers.cycle_count.current // 0) >= (.triggers.cycle_count.limit // $th.cycles)
308	        then ["cycle_count", "\(.triggers.cycle_count.current) changes-required rounds (derived from the feedback history)"]
309	      else null end ) as $trip
310	  | if $trip != null and (.state // "CLOSED") != "OPEN"
311	    then .state = "OPEN" | .history = ((.history // []) + [{timestamp: $ts, trigger: $trip[0], reason: $trip[1], source: "derive"}])
312	    else .state = (.state // "CLOSED") end;
313	def known_ids: (.derivation.sprint_ids // null) // ((.sprints.list // []) | map(.id? // empty));
314	def resolve($f; $now; $win):
315	  . as $c
316	  | (if ($c | type) == "object" then $c else {} end) as $c
317	  | ($c.state // $c.status // "") as $cs
318	  | ($c | known_ids) as $known
319	  | ([$f.sprints[] | select(.state != "complete")
320	      | "sprint-\(.global_id)" as $g | .local_label as $l
321	      | select(($known | index($g)) == null and ($l == "" or ($known | index($l)) == null))] | length > 0) as $new
322	  | ((($c.completion // {}) | .merged_sha? // "") | type == "string" and length > 0) as $merged
323	  | if ($c.state // "") == "JACKED_OUT" or ($c.status // "") == "JACKED_OUT" or $merged then "JACKED_OUT"
324	    elif $f.breaker_open or $cs == "HALTED" then "HALTED"
325	    elif $f.all_complete then "COMPLETE"
326	    elif $cs == "COMPLETE" and ($new | not) then "COMPLETE"
327	    elif ($c.timestamps.last_activity? // null) | fresh($now; $win) then "RUNNING"
328	    else "INTERRUPTED" end;
329	'

Now I found an issue! Looking at line 74 in karpathy-surgical-diff-check.sh:

```bash
switch="$(loa_knob karpathy_principles.surgical_diff_warning true 2>/dev/null)"
```

The fallback is `true` (a boolean), but loa_knob expects string falllback arguments. When the config key is missing, it returns "true", but that is semantically confusing since the fallback should probably be `false` to match what happens when the knob is off. But more importantly, the code at line 76 then checks:

```bash
case "$switch" in
    false|False|FALSE|0|no|No|NO|off|Off|OFF) exit 0 ;;
esac
```

So if the key is missing/not set and the fallback is `true`, the script continues (which is correct). However, there's still a logical issue on line 74: the fallback value is `true` but that gets returned as a string. Let me verify this is intentional behavior by checking how it's used. Actually, looking at line 76, that seems correct - if switch is `true`, it doesn't match any of the false values, so it continues. So this might actually be OK.

+# table-header lines between it and the start marker, the marker block, and
+# one blank line after the end marker. A file without the start marker is

Failing scenario: a reviewer running `grep 'hash:' .claude/skills/*/SKILL.md | grep input_guardrails` would see six different values for one include, indicating the markers were not regenerated after changes. While fallback `-f` format works, the format incompatibility on line 83 (${st//$'\n'/;}) silently swallows newlines without validating all three files' stat outputs are present. +#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# =============================================================================
+# tools/check-knob-readers.sh — no direct read of a profile key outside
+# profile-lib.sh (cycle-129 SDD D-9.1, sprint-256 Task 2.7).
+#
+# Every key under any profile in .claude/data/profiles.yaml must be read
+# through `loa_knob` (.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh), never by a reader's
+# own `yq '.<key> // <default>'`: a direct read skips the profile, and yq's
+# `//` reads an explicit `false` as absent. The check flags a line that names a
+# profile key in yq-path form (a leading dot: `.guardrails.input.enabled`)
+# under .claude/ (scripts, hooks, skills, data) and tools/, except
+# profile-lib.sh itself. Prose that names a key without the dot
+# (`guardrails.input.enabled: false`) is not a read and is not flagged.
+#
+# Misses: a key assembled at runtime (".guardrails.input.${x}.enabled") and a
+# reader in a language that indexes the config as nested keys.
+#
+# Usage: tools/check-knob-readers.sh [--root DIR]
+# Exit:  0 clean · 1 direct read found (each printed as path:line) · 2 usage
+# =============================================================================
+set -euo pipefail
+export LC_ALL=C
+
+ROOT="."
+while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
+  case "$1" in
+    --root) [[ $# -ge 2 ]] || { echo "check-knob-readers.sh: --root needs a directory" >&2; exit 2; }; ROOT="$2"; shift 2 ;;
+    -h|--help) sed -n '/^# Usage:/,/^# Exit:/p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; exit 0 ;;
+    *) echo "check-knob-readers.sh: unknown arg $1" >&2; exit 2 ;;
+  esac
+done
+PROFILES="$ROOT/.claude/data/profiles.yaml"
+[[ -f "$PROFILES" ]] || { echo "check-knob-readers.sh: $PROFILES not found" >&2; exit 2; }
+command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "check-knob-readers.sh: yq v4 required" >&2; exit 2; }
+
+keys=$(yq -r '.profiles[] | keys | .[]' "$PROFILES" | sort -u)
+[[ -n "$keys" ]] || { echo "check-knob-readers.sh: no profile keys in $PROFILES" >&2; exit 2; }
+# Alternation of the dot-escaped keys; each must be preceded by a dot that is
+# not itself part of an identifier (start of line, quote, space, paren, ...).
+alt=$(printf '%s\n' "$keys" | sed 's/\./\\./g' | paste -sd'|' -)
+pattern="(^|[^A-Za-z0-9_])\\.(${alt})([^A-Za-z0-9_]|$)"
+
+hits=$(cd "$ROOT" && grep -rnE "$pattern" .claude tools 2>/dev/null \
+  | grep -v -E '^(\./)?\.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib\.sh:' \
+  | grep -v -E '^(\./)?tools/check-knob-readers\.sh:' || true)
+if [[ -n "$hits" ]]; then
+  echo "check-knob-readers.sh: direct read(s) of a profile key; use loa_knob from .claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh:" >&2
+  printf '%s\n' "$hits" | cut -c1-240 >&2
+  exit 1
+fi
+echo "check-knob-readers.sh: no direct profile-key reads ($(printf '%s\n' "$keys" | wc -l | tr -d ' ') keys checked)"

@@ -0,0 +1,51 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# =============================================================================
+# tools/check-knob-readers.sh — no direct read of a profile key outside
+# profile-lib.sh (cycle-129 SDD D-9.1, sprint-256 Task 2.7).
+#
+# Every key under any profile in .claude/data/profiles.yaml must be read
+# through `loa_knob` (.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh), never by a reader's
+# own `yq '.<key> // <default>'`: a direct read skips the profile, and yq's
+# `//` reads an explicit `false` as absent. The check flags a line that names a
+# profile key in yq-path form (a leading dot: `.guardrails.input.enabled`)
+# under .claude/ (scripts, hooks, skills, data) and tools/, except
+# profile-lib.sh itself. Prose that names a key without the dot
+# (`guardrails.input.enabled: false`) is not a read and is not flagged.
+#
+# Misses: a key assembled at runtime (".guardrails.input.${x}.enabled") and a
+# reader in a language that indexes the config as nested keys.
+#
+# Usage: tools/check-knob-readers.sh [--root DIR]
+# Exit:  0 clean · 1 direct read found (each printed as path:line) · 2 usage
+# =============================================================================
+set -euo pipefail
+export LC_ALL=C
+
+ROOT="."
+while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
+  case "$1" in
+    --root) [[ $# -ge 2 ]] || { echo "check-knob-readers.sh: --root needs a directory" >&2; exit 2; }; ROOT="$2"; shift 2 ;;
+    -h|--help) sed -n '/^# Usage:/,/^# Exit:/p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; exit 0 ;;
+    *) echo "check-knob-readers.sh: unknown arg $1" >&2; exit 2 ;;
+  esac
+done
+PROFILES="$ROOT/.claude/data/profiles.yaml"
+[[ -f "$PROFILES" ]] || { echo "check-knob-readers.sh: $PROFILES not found" >&2; exit 2; }
+command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "check-knob-readers.sh: yq v4 required" >&2; exit 2; }
+
+keys=$(yq -r '.profiles[] | keys | .[]' "$PROFILES" | sort -u)
+[[ -n "$keys" ]] || { echo "check-knob-readers.sh: no profile keys in $PROFILES" >&2; exit 2; }
+# Alternation of the dot-escaped keys; each must be preceded by a dot that is
+# not itself part of an identifier (start of line, quote, space, paren, ...).
+alt=$(printf '%s\n' "$keys" | sed 's/\./\\./g' | paste -sd'|' -)
+pattern="(^|[^A-Za-z0-9_])\\.(${alt})([^A-Za-z0-9_]|$)"
+
+hits=$(cd "$ROOT" && grep -rnE "$pattern" .claude tools 2>/dev/null \
+  | grep -v -E '^(\./)?\.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib\.sh:' \
+  | grep -v -E '^(\./)?tools/check-knob-readers\.sh:' || true)
+if [[ -n "$hits" ]]; then
+  echo "check-knob-readers.sh: direct read(s) of a profile key; use loa_knob from .claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh:" >&2
+  printf '%s\n' "$hits" | cut -c1-240 >&2
+  exit 1
+fi
+echo "check-knob-readers.sh: no direct profile-key reads ($(printf '%s\n' "$keys" | wc -l | tr -d ' ') keys checked)"
